A JSON payload’s numbers that a double cannot hold

Trystero JS

A JSON payload is sent as JSON.stringify writes a JavaScript value, whose numbers are doubles: JSON.parse reads an integer past 253, or a decimal of more digits than a double keeps, as the nearest double, and a number past a double’s range as Infinity, which JSON.stringify writes as null.

trystero

A webcpp::document::document holds each number exactly, and a room sends it as the document writes it, each number a double holds as JavaScript writes it. A Trystero JS peer that receives the payload reads the nearest double, or Infinity.

Why

webcpp::document keeps every number exact, and writes each one a double holds as JavaScript does.

// The numbers of the payload's JSON text, none of which a double holds: an integer past 2^53,
// a decimal of 34 digits, and a number past a double's range.
constexpr std::array<std::string_view, 3> numbers{
    "9007199254740993",
    "0.1000000000000000000000000000000001",
    "1e999",
};
std::string text = "[";
for (const std::string_view number : numbers) {
    text += text.size() > 1 ? "," : "";
    text += number;
}
text += ']';
// This room sends the payload its JSON text makes, once it meets the other peer.
auto payload = room.make_action<wd::document>("payload");
room.on_peer_join([&](std::string_view) {
    wd::result<wd::document> value = wd::parse(text);
    if (!value) {
        std::cerr << "not parsed: " << value.error().message() << '\n';
        leave();
        return;
    }
    payload.async_send(std::move(*value), [](boost::system::error_code) {});
});
// What the other peer receives, number by number.
auto received = other->make_action<wd::document>("payload");
received.on_message([&](const wd::document& value, const trystero::message_info&) {
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < numbers.size(); ++i) {
        std::cout << numbers[i] << " arrives as " << value[i].stringify() << '\n';
    }
    leave();
});
The twin, on Trystero JS
import {joinRoom} from 'trystero'
import {RTCPeerConnection} from 'werift'
import {openPage} from '../page.mjs'

// The peers meet on this machine alone: no ICE server, werift's WebRTC for Node.
const config = {
    appId: 'webcpp-trystero-differences',
    relayConfig: {urls: [process.env.TRYSTERO_RELAY_URL]},
    rtcConfig: {iceServers: []},
}
// The other peer, another page, which posts what it receives for this page to print.
const other = openPage(async ({joinRoom, RTCPeerConnection, data, post, next}) => {
    const room = joinRoom({...data, rtcPolyfill: RTCPeerConnection}, 'lobby')
    room.makeAction('payload').onMessage = received => post(received)
    await next()
    await room.leave()
}, config)
const room = joinRoom({...config, rtcPolyfill: RTCPeerConnection}, 'lobby')

// tag::example[]
// The numbers of the payload's JSON text, none of which a double holds: an integer past 2^53, a
// decimal of 34 digits, and a number past a double's range.
const numbers = ['9007199254740993', '0.1000000000000000000000000000000001', '1e999']
const text = `[${numbers.join(',')}]`
// This page sends the payload its JSON text makes, once it meets the other peer.
const payload = room.makeAction('payload')
await new Promise(joined => (room.onPeerJoin = joined))
await payload.send(JSON.parse(text))
// What the other peer receives, number by number.
const received = await other.next()
numbers.forEach((number, i) => console.log(`${number} arrives as ${JSON.stringify(received[i])}`))
// end::example[]
other.post('leave')
await Promise.all([room.leave(), other.done])

A JSON payload nested deeper than 256, holding a lone surrogate, or past the room’s bound

Trystero JS

JSON.parse reads a payload nested deeper than 256, a string that holds a lone surrogate, "\ud800", as JSON.stringify writes one, and an array of any length, so a room delivers all three.

trystero

A room reads a JSON payload with webcpp::document’s defaults, into an image of at most room_options::max_json_document_bytes, 64 MiB by default, and delivers none: a text nested deeper than 256 is refused, and so is a lone surrogate, and an array of 1,000 zeros, whose nodes need some 190 KB, in a room whose bound is 64 KiB. The room goes on, and delivers the payloads sent after them.

Why

webcpp::document’s defaults: a bounded depth, and strings that are UTF-8; and each value of a document is a node of 192 bytes of image, 96 times its text at most, so a program bounds what a peer’s JSON may take of its room’s resource. Every payload within the bound is delivered: its image is first bounded by 96 times its length and 64 KiB, which every valid text fits (JSON texts).

The program’s room sets the bound:

// A room whose received JSON payloads take at most 64 KiB of its resource each.
auto joined = app.join("lobby", {.max_json_document_bytes = std::uint64_t{64} << 10U});

A Trystero JS page sends such payloads, and no C++ peer sends a lone surrogate, which a document’s UTF-8 strings cannot hold. So the program’s other peer sends what a page sends: each payload’s JSON text, as JSON.stringify writes the value, as a text payload, which the backend its app is given marks as JSON on the wire.

// The payloads the other peer sends, as JSON text, each an array of its label and a value: one
// nested 257 deep, one holding a lone surrogate, an array of 1,000 zeros past the room's bound,
// and a last one sent after them.
std::string zeros = "[0";
for (std::size_t i = 1; i < 1000; ++i) {
    zeros += ",0";
}
const auto payloads = std::to_array<std::pair<std::string_view, std::string>>({
    {"nested 257 deep", std::string(256, '[') + std::string(256, ']')},
    {"holding a lone surrogate", R"("\ud800")"},
    {"of 1,000 zeros", zeros + "]"},
    {"sent after them", R"("plain")"},
});
// What this room delivers of them, by label, once the last has come.
auto payload = room.make_action<wd::document>(action_name);
std::vector<std::string> delivered;
payload.on_message([&](const wd::document& value, const trystero::message_info&) {
    delivered.emplace_back(value[0].value_or(std::string_view()));
    if (delivered.back() != payloads.back().first) {
        return;
    }
    for (const auto& sent : payloads) {
        const bool came = std::ranges::find(delivered, sent.first) != delivered.end();
        std::cout << "the payload " << sent.first << ": "
                  << (came ? "delivered" : "not delivered") << '\n';
    }
    leave();
});
The twin, on Trystero JS
import {joinRoom} from 'trystero'
import {RTCPeerConnection} from 'werift'
import {openPage} from '../page.mjs'

// The peers meet on this machine alone: no ICE server, werift's WebRTC for Node.
const config = {
    appId: 'webcpp-trystero-differences',
    relayConfig: {urls: [process.env.TRYSTERO_RELAY_URL]},
    rtcConfig: {iceServers: []},
}
// The payloads the other peer sends, as JSON text, each an array of its label and a value: one
// nested 257 deep, one holding a lone surrogate, an array of 1,000 zeros, and a last one sent
// after them.
const payloads = [
    ['nested 257 deep', '['.repeat(256) + ']'.repeat(256)],
    ['holding a lone surrogate', '"\\ud800"'],
    ['of 1,000 zeros', JSON.stringify(new Array(1000).fill(0))],
    ['sent after them', '"plain"'],
]
// The other peer, another page, which sends each payload JSON.parse makes of its text once it
// meets this page, each once the one before is sent.
const other = openPage(async ({joinRoom, RTCPeerConnection, data: {config, texts}, next}) => {
    const room = joinRoom({...config, rtcPolyfill: RTCPeerConnection}, 'lobby')
    const payload = room.makeAction('payload')
    await new Promise(joined => (room.onPeerJoin = joined))
    for (const text of texts) await payload.send(JSON.parse(text))
    await next()
    await room.leave()
}, {config, texts: payloads.map(([label, value]) => `["${label}",${value}]`)})
const room = joinRoom({...config, rtcPolyfill: RTCPeerConnection}, 'lobby')

// tag::example[]
// What this page delivers of them, by label, once the last has come.
const payload = room.makeAction('payload')
const delivered = []
await new Promise(last => {
    payload.onMessage = ([label]) => {
        delivered.push(label)
        if (label === payloads.at(-1)[0]) last()
    }
})
for (const [label] of payloads) {
    console.log(`the payload ${label}: ${delivered.includes(label) ? 'delivered' : 'not delivered'}`)
}
// end::example[]
other.post('leave')
await Promise.all([room.leave(), other.done])

A self id that is not UTF-8

Trystero JS

Has none: it draws its selfId when its module loads and takes none from a program.

trystero

An app given a self id that is not UTF-8 sets it aside for 20 random characters, and reports error::invalid_configuration to app::on_error.

Why

JSON carries UTF-8 alone, and a signal writes the id as a JSON string.

This program has no twin, since no program of Trystero’s can give it an id (test/oracle/twins/without-twin.txt), and it joins no room, so it needs no relay: it runs with the ordinary examples.

const std::string given = "caf\xE9";  // ISO 8859-1's "café": its last byte is no UTF-8
trystero::app_config config;
config.app_id = "webcpp-trystero-differences";
config.self_id = given;
trystero::app app(io.get_executor(), backend, std::move(config));
app.on_error([](std::string_view, boost::system::error_code ec, std::string_view what) {
    std::cout << "reported: " << ec.message() << ": " << what << '\n';
});
std::cout << "the self id given: " << given.size() << " bytes, not UTF-8\n"
          << "the app's self id: "
          << (app.self_id() == given
                  ? std::string("the one given")
                  : std::to_string(app.self_id().size()) + " random characters")
          << '\n';
trystero prints
the self id given: 4 bytes, not UTF-8
the app's self id: 20 random characters
reported: the configuration is unusable: self_id is not UTF-8, which no peer reads, so the app uses a random one

The differences no program shows

These rows of Where a ported feature behaves otherwise have no program, each for its reason.

Behaviour Why no program shows it

A peer kicked from a room, or that kicked us, over a live connection; frames after the higher id’s own kick; a connection whose last room was kicked

A kick follows a room proof that fails over a live connection, and two C++ apps never send one: an app has one password for every room, and apps of different passwords share no connection. A Trystero JS page that mixes passwords does, so the interop lane’s wrong room proofs show trystero’s side, against a page and not a twin (The oracle and the interop lanes), and the shared test holds the rest over the memory relays.

Reuse over a live connection

Only a forged announcement shows it: a third party that publishes, in a peer’s name, a room token that peer never advertised, which neither API publishes. The shared test forges one over the memory relays.

A room frame before the peer’s presence for the room

Both APIs advertise a room before its first frame on a connection, so only a presence lost on the way shows it: Chrome drops it, rarely, when a page sends as its answering channel opens, and the interop lane’s delayed-open scenario met it; the connection and shared tests drop it over the memory relays.

Announcements after a peer leaves

What differs is what a room publishes to its relays after a peer leaves it while their connection stays, which neither API reports: the peers see the same joins and leaves.

Presence after binding

A frame on the connection, which neither API reports; what it changes is how soon the other side binds, a time that no two runs print alike.

An answer to an earlier challenge

It needs a handshake answer that arrives after a newer challenge, a race between two bindings that no program sets up on a real network; the shared test holds it over the memory relays, whose frames it holds and releases.

Relay sockets and the Nostr key: the key

Which key signs a room’s events only the relay sees; neither a room nor a peer reports it. The sockets are shown (Relay sockets).

idle_timeout

Not a behaviour: both keep an idle connection 123,333 ms, and Trystero JS takes the same setting under its test-only name, so a program and its twin would agree.

Frames waiting for a bound room’s handler

A state Trystero JS passes through between a binding and its room’s data handler, which its rooms set as they bind; no program reaches it through the API.

Renegotiation and media over a shared connection; passive rooms

Not ported: trystero has nothing of them to run.

Duplicate connections

Only two connections whose channels open within a millisecond of each other, from two rooms meeting the peer at once, make a pair that is crossed, which no program sets up on demand: the interop lane’s two-room scenarios meet one now and then, and the app_impl and shared tests hold each outcome over the memory relays.

A Nostr event a relay repeats, or that several relays carry

What an event changes when it comes twice is the signaling’s work, offers and answers made again, which neither API reports: a program sees one join either way, and over honest relays an event’s id is always its own. The protocol and room tests hold the dedup, forged ids included.

A relay’s text, a signal or a handshake message past its bound; a protocol text of thousands of values, or nested deeper than 16

No Trystero peer writes such a text, so only a relay or a peer that means harm sends one, and what changes is whether the room reads it, which neither API reports. The protocol and signaling tests hold the bounds.

The characters of a random id

A bias of about 0.005 bits a character, which only a count over many ids shows, and a count of random characters prints something else on every run.

Appendix B: Roadmap

What trystero does not port yet, and what it does not build itself yet (Differences from Trystero gives each feature left out with its reason):

  1. Media. Audio and video tracks and streams, and Trystero’s @_stream, @_track and @_signal actions with renegotiation. In the browser they are the page’s MediaStreamTrack objects. Natively they would be libdatachannel’s RTP tracks, whose encoding, decoding and capture are the application’s. What that needs was measured: libdatachannel keeps only weak references to tracks, answers with every codec offered unless the answer is pruned, and echoes the offerer’s msid into the answer. Media will be an interface of webcpp::webrtc’s, which the backends’ WebRTC is.

  2. Trystero’s other features. Request actions (kind: 'request'), decisions on incoming transfers and their progress, the application’s own handshake, passive rooms, and the other strategies, among them MQTT and BitTorrent trackers.

Appendix C: Acknowledgements

trystero ports the wire protocol of Trystero 0.26.0, Copyright (c) 2021 Dan Motzenbecker, so that its rooms are Trystero’s rooms. It was written with Trystero’s source open: its protocol constants, its message layouts, its default relays in their order, with the shuffle that derives an app’s relays from its id, and its default STUN servers come from it. Trystero is distributed under the MIT License, whose text and copyright notice are in LICENSE-TRYSTERO.txt, at the root of the library, exactly as Trystero 0.26.0 ships them. That adds no licence to trystero’s own code, which is under the Boost Software License alone.

The BIP-340 signatures of the Nostr events are libsecp256k1's, by the Bitcoin Core contributors, under the MIT License. The platform backend’s WebRTC is, natively, webcpp::webrtc’s over libdatachannel, by Paul-Louis Ageneau, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0.

Appendix D: Changelog

What changed in trystero in each version of webcpp, newest first, one line per change. "Unreleased" is what the next version brings. The release notes of every version are on webcpp’s index page.

Unreleased

  • Breaking change: Changed native:: and browser:: to one platform::backend (link /webcpp/trystero//platform), and a backend’s now_ms() and unix_seconds() to steady_now() and unix_now(), of std::chrono.

  • Breaking change: Changed trystero’s Asio to webcpp::asio; a page’s main runs its io_context under a work guard, and calls in through platform::page_call of platform/page.hpp.

  • Breaking change: Changed JSON payloads to webcpp::document::document and webcpp::document::pmr::document, sent as JSON.stringify writes them, for boost::json::value and json_resource; payload has no copy assignment, and programs link Boost.Charconv too.

  • Breaking change: Changed relays to verify TLS in any verify mode, drop binary messages, and refuse URLs a page reads otherwise and TLS contexts a page cannot honour.

  • Breaking change: Changed protocol:: to take webcpp::document’s values, removing json::parse and make_id; append_string returns its error, and proposal::size is a std::uint64_t.

  • Breaking change: Changed libsecp256k1 to /third_party//secp256k1, with webcpp-secp256k1-tables for its tables and no -sSECP256K1_ROOT, and app::join to [[nodiscard]].

  • Fixed relays hiding a genuine Nostr event, slowing rooms with colliding ids or making them read 8 MiB refusals, rooms dropping or piling up simultaneous offers, and MSVC 14.52 builds.

  • Added room_options::max_json_document_bytes for a received JSON payload; every JSON text is read in the room’s resource within bounds, and a self id not UTF-8 is replaced by a random one.

  • Fixed unreachable IPv6 relays, signals unlike Trystero’s, 32-bit receivers misreading 4 GiB offers, pages ignoring failing crypto.getRandomValues or dropping early frames, unbound rooms after lost presence, and crossed-connection peer errors.

  • Changed the quick start to one native program, and added programs showing differences beside Trystero JS’s output.

webcpp 0.1.0

  • Fixed native multiroom handoffs losing early presence frames, and negotiations stalled by a channel closing before room binding.

  • Changed the native backend to build pinned libdatachannel sources and their dependencies through B2, sharing source-built OpenSSL with Asio and Beast.

  • Changed native builds to require threading=multi; the backend uses workers.

  • Fixed GCC compilation of native WebSocket coroutine callbacks.

  • Changed room construction to app::join, sharing connections between rooms.

  • Breaking change: Removed room_config; construct app and use join with app_config and room_options.

  • Breaking change: Changed passwords to app_config; different passwords require separate apps and self ids.

  • Added a changelog, the page’s last appendix, with each version’s changes.

  • Changed config.hpp to include <webcpp/config.hpp>, webcpp’s configuration, which the build adds.

  • Added WEBCPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS, which disables trystero’s exceptions with every webcpp library’s.
